title: Attorney General Bonta issues alert on misleading health care sharing ministry plans
text:
Attorney General Bonta issues alert on misleading health care sharing ministry plans
California Attorney General Rob Bonta issued a consumer alert on July 29 reminding Californians about misleading claims made by some health care sharing ministries, also known as HCSMs. The alert comes amid rising health insurance premiums and coverage losses following the expiration of enhanced premium subsidies under the Affordable Care Act at the end of 2025.
Bonta said, “Health care sharing ministries do not provide the same protections as Covered California plans, and that difference can matter the most in times of medical need. Without comprehensive health insurance, an unexpected illness or serious accident could leave you responsible for substantial medical bills. Even as congressional Republicans and the Trump Administration continue to undermine the Affordable Care Act, Covered California plans can still provide affordable, quality health insurance options, giving Californians access to the coverage they deserve.”
According to Bonta’s office, some HCSMs are advertising their plans as affordable alternatives to ACA-compliant healthcare coverage but do not guarantee coverage for preexisting conditions or essential services. The Attorney General’s Office has reached settlements with Alliance for Shared Health, Sedera Inc., and The Aliera Companies Inc., requiring them to stop selling these types of plans in California due to misleading practices. However, officials warn that other entities may still be operating illegally by selling unlicensed insurance without required consumer protections.
The alert advises consumers to carefully review disclosures and member guidelines when considering an HCSM plan. It highlights that many HCSMs use language similar to traditional insurance products—such as labeling offerings as gold, silver or bronze “plans”—which can cause confusion among consumers who may only realize they have enrolled in an HCSM after a claim is denied. Consumers are urged to consider financial risks associated with limited or excluded coverage for preexisting conditions and essential benefits like mental healthcare or maternity care.
Bonta continues efforts against federal policies he says drive up healthcare costs. In March 2026, he co-led a coalition opposing a proposed rule from federal agencies that would reduce enrollment and increase out-of-pocket expenses; in July 2025, he joined litigation challenging another rule seen as creating barriers under the ACA.
Rob Bonta leads the California Attorney General's office, which serves as chief law enforcement authority across California's executive branch and advances initiatives in civil rights, consumer protection and environmental justice according to the official website.
